## Raman Peak Fitting — Results

**Main fitted peak positions** (strongest first):

| Band | Center (cm⁻¹) | Rel. intensity | Assignment |

| Lattice/external mode | **150.8** ± 0.6 | 0.012 | external mode |

**Baseline:** flat, rolling-min area fraction 0.077 → negligible fluorescence.

### Interpretation
The band pattern is diagnostic of the **sulfate anion (SO₄²⁻)** internal modes. The specific set — ν₁ ≈ 988, ν₂ ≈ 461, ν₄ ≈ 617 cm⁻¹ — matches **barite (BaSO₄)**, and clearly distinguishes it from gypsum (ν₁ ≈ 1008) and anhydrite (ν₁ ≈ 1017). The identification rests on the coincidence of the three strongest bands (ν₁/ν₂/ν₄), not just the dominant peak.

### Caveats
- **Pattern-only ID:** no elemental data (EDX/XRF) was provided, so the BaSO₄ assignment is spectroscopic. It is well constrained, but a cation confirmation would clinch it.
- The tall ν₁ band shows a dispersive residual (~87× noise) → real lineshape **asymmetry**. The fit's ~981 and ~448 cm⁻¹ "shoulder" components are accounting devices absorbing that asymmetry, **not** confirmed distinct vibrational modes.
- Two unassigned minor features (~190 cm⁻¹ sharp spike; ~1103 cm⁻¹ near noise floor) — likely a second lattice mode and/or a cosmic-ray artifact; neither affects the identification.
